definition: A lipooligosaccharide consisting of a phenolic phthiocerol core linked to the trisaccharide 3,6-di-O-methyl-α-D-glucopyranosyl-(1→4)-2,3-di-O-methyl-α-L-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→2)-3-O-methyl-α-L-rhamnopyranose.

name: phenolic phthiocerol
definition: A lipid derived from phthiocerol, having a 4-hydroxyphenyl substituent at the 29-position.

name: phthiocerol A
definition: A lipid-based glycol consisting of (3S,4R)-3-methoxy-4-methylnonacosane having (9R)- and (11S)-hydroxy substituents; a characteristic constituent of the waxes of tubercule bacilli.

name: 4,6-dideoxy-4-(3-deoxy-L-glycero-tetronamido)-α-D-Manp2Me-(1→2)-4,6-dideoxy-4-(3-deoxy-L-glycero-tetronamido)-α-D-ManpOMe
definition: An amido disaccharide fragment which mimicks the terminus of the O-polysaccharide of Vibrio cholerae O:1, serotype Ogawa (PDB entry: 1F4Y).

name: flucofuron
definition: A member of the class of phenylureas that is urea in which each nitrogen is substituted by a 4-chloro-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group.

name: (R)-bendroflumethiazide
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of bendroflumethiazide.

name: (S)-bendroflumethiazide
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of bendroflumethiazide.

name: 5-amino-2-chlorobenzotrifluoride
definition: A monochlorobenzene that is the 3-trifluoromethyl derivative of 4-chloroaniline.

name: sulcofuron
definition: An organochlorine pesticide consisting of 1,3-diphenylurea having chloro substituents at the 3-, 4- and 5'-positions and a 4-chloro-2-sulfophenoxy group at the 2'-position.

name: sulcofuron-sodium
definition: The sodium salt of sulcofuron.

name: sulcofuronate
definition: Conjugate base of sulcofuron.

name: α-D-Manp-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→2)-D-Manp
definition: A tetrasaccharide comprising four mannosyl residues joined by α(1→2) linkages.

name: β-D-Manp-(1→2)-β-D-Manp-(1→2)-β-D-Manp-(1→2)-D-Manp
definition: A tetrasaccharide comprising four D-mannose residues joined by β(1→2) linkages.

name: (R)-betaxolol
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of betaxolol.

name: (S)-betaxolol
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of betaxolol.

name: (R)-betaxolol hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of (R)-betaxolol.

name: (S)-betaxolol hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of (S)-betaxolol.

name: α-D-Glcp-(1→3)-[L-α-D-Hepp-(1→7)]-L-α-D-Hepp-4P
definition: A trisaccharide derivative and oligosaccharide phosphate comprised of one α-D-glucopyranosyl and two L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptopyranosyl residues. The sequence is present in enterobacterial lipopolysaccharide from all E. coli, Salmonella and Shigella.

name: 3,6-dideoxy-4-C-(1,3-dimethoxy-4,5,6,7-tetrahydroxyheptyl)-α-D-xylo-hexp-(1→3)-β-L-Xylp
definition: A glycosylxylose derivative that comprises the highly antigenic lipooligosaccharide, LOS-III, epitope of Mycobacterium gastri.

name: (R)-bethanechol
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of bethanechol.

name: (S)-bethanechol
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of bethanechol.

name: (R)-bethanechol chloride
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of bethanechol chloride.

name: (S)-bethanechol chloride
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of bethanechol chloride.

name: palmitelaidic acid
definition: A straight-chain, monounsaturated, 16-carbon fatty acid with a trans-double bond at position C-9; the trans-isomer of palmitoleic acid and predominant trans-16:1 isomer in cheeses from goat and ewe milk. Major dietary sources are partly hydrogenated vegetable oils.
An amido pentasaccharide fragment which mimicks the terminus of the O-polysaccharide of Vibrio cholerae O:1, serotype Ogawa.

name: dexbrompheniramine
definition: The (pharmacologically active) (S)-(+)-enantiomer of brompheniramine. A histamine H1 receptor antagonist, it is used (commonly as its maleate salt) for the symptomatic relief of allergic conditions, including rhinitis and conjunctivitis.

name: 2-hydroxymyristic acid
definition: A long-chain fatty acid that is a derivative of myristic acid having a hydroxy substituent at C-2.

name: γ-D-glutamyl-meso-diaminopimelic acid
definition: The γ-D-glutamyl derivative of meso-diaminopimelic acid. Minimal ligand of NOD1.

name: 4,6-dideoxy-4-(2-methoxypropanamido)-3-C-Me-L-Manp2Me-(1→3)-Fucp
definition: An amido disaccharide comprising 4,6-dideoxy-4-(2-methoxypropanamido)-3-C-methyl-2-O-methyl-L-mannopyranose linked through the anomeric carbon to the 3-hydroxy group of L-fucose.

name: dexbrompheniramine maleate
definition: The maleic acid salt of the (pharmacologically active) (S)-(+)-enantiomer of brompheniramine. A histamine H1 receptor antagonist, it is used for the symptomatic relief of allergic conditions, including rhinitis and conjunctivitis.

name: methyl L-xylopyranoside
definition: The methyl glycoside of L-xylopyranose.

name: L-xylopyranose
definition: The pyranose form of L-xylose.

name: D-quinovosamine
definition: D-glucosamine deoxygenated at C-6.

name: N-acetyl-D-quinovosamine
definition: D-Quinovosamine acetylated on the amino nitrogen.

name: 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-α-L-galactopyranuronosyl-(1→3)-N-acetyl-D-quinovosamine
definition: A disaccharide formed by an α1→3 glycosidic linkage between N-acetyl-L-galactosaminuronic acid and N-acetylquinovosamine.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-D-Galp-(1→3)-α-D-GlcNAc-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap
definition: A tetrasaccharide derivative consisting of α-L-rhamnose, α-D-galactose, N-acetyl-α-D-glucosamine and α-L-rhamnose residues in a linear (1→2, (1→3), (1→3) sequence.

name: α-L-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→2)-α-D-galactopyranose
definition: A disaccharide consisting of α-L-rhamnose and α-D-galactose linked via a 1→2 glycosidic bond.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-D-Galp
definition: A trisaccharide consisting of two α-L-rhamnose residues and an α-D-galactose residue in a linear (1→3), (1→2) sequence.

name: E. coli strain F470 LPS core oligosaccharide 1
definition: A branched twelve-membered oligosaccharide phosphate consisting of two galactose residues, three glucose residues, two 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid residues, three L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose residues and two glucosamine residues, one of which is at the reducing end. The unit constitutes one of the two core oligosaccharide structures of enterobacterial lipopolysaccharide obtained from E. coli strain F470.

name: α-tyvelopyranosyl-(1→3)-α-D-mannopyranose
definition: A glycosylmannose consisting of α-D-mannopyranose having a tyvelopyranosyl residue attached via an α-(1→3)-linkage

name: (R)-butaconazole
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of butaconazole.

name: (S)-butoconazole
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of butoconazole.

name: (R)-butoconazole nitrate
definition: The nitric acid salt of (R)-butoconazole.

name: (S)-butoconazole nitrate
definition: The nitric acid salt of (S)-butoconazole.

name: α-Kdo-(2→8)-α-Kdo
definition: A disaccharide consisting of two 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulopyranonosyl units joined via an α-(2→8)-linkage.

name: α-Kdo-(2→8)-α-Kdo-(2→4)-α-Kdo
definition: A trisaccharide consisting of three 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulopyranonosyl units in a linear sequence.

name: α-D-GlcNAc-(1→2)-α-D-Glc-(1→2)-α-D-Gal-(1→3)-[α-D-Gal-(1→6)]-α-D-Glc-(1→3)-[L-glycero-α-D-manno-Hep-(1→7)]-L-glycero-α-D-manno-Hep-(1→3)-L-glycero-D-manno-Hep
definition: An oligosaccharide derivative that is a branched octasaccharide derivative consisting of two galactose residues, three glucose residues, one N-acetylglucosamine residue and three L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose residues, one of which is at the reducing end. The unit constitutes one of the core oligosaccharide structures of enterobacterial lipopolysaccharide obtained from Salmonella species.

name: α-L-Fucp-(1→3)-[β-D-Galp-(1→4)]-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: An α-L-Fucp-(1→3)-[β-D-Galp-(1→4)]-D-GlcpNAc where the glucosamine at the reducing end has β-configuration at its anomeric centre. Commonly known as Lewis x trisaccharide or Lex.

name: β-D-Galp-(1→3)-[α-L-Fucp-(1→4)]-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: A β-D-Galp-(1→3)-[α-L-Fucp-(1→4)]-D-GlcpNAc where the N-acetyl-D-glucosamine at the reducing end has β-configuration at its anomeric centre.

name: α-L-Fucp-(1→2)-β-D-Galp-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: An amino trisaccharide consisting of α-L-fucose, β-D-galactose and N-acetyl-β-D-glucosamine residues joined by sequential (1→2)- and (1→3)-linkages.

name: benzylpenicilloyl polylysine
definition: Poly-L-lysine (n > 40) in which 50-70% of the ε-amino groups are substituted with benzylpenicilloyl groups. It is used as a skin-testing reagent to detect immunoglobulin E antibodies in people with a history of penicillin allergy.

name: α-4-(3-deoxy-L-glycero-tetronoyl)amino-4,6-dideoxy-D-mannose-(1→2)-α-4-(3-deoxy-L-glycero-tetronoyl)-amino-4,6-dideoxy-D-mannose
definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of two 4-amino-4,6-dideoxy-D-mannose residues joined by an α-(1→2)-linkage.

name: α-D-Kdo-(2→8)-α-D-Kdo-(2→6)-β-D-GlcNAc
definition: A trisaccharide consisting of two 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulose residues and a single N-acetylglucosamine residue in a linear sequence, joined via α-linkages.

name: (R)-bromazine
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of bromazine.

name: (S)-bromazine
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of bromazine.

name: α-D-Kdo-(2→4)-α-D-Kdo-(2→4)-α-D-Kdo-(2→6)-β-D-GlcNAc
definition: A tetrasaccharide consisting of three 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulose residues and a single N-acetylglucosamine residue in a linear sequence, joined via α-linkages.

name: (R)-bromazine hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of (R)-bromazine.

name: (S)-bromazine hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of (S)-bromazine.

name: α-D-Kdo-(2→4)-α-D-Kdo-(2→8)-α-D-Kdo-(2→4)-α-D-Kdo
definition: A tetrasaccharide consisting of four 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulose residues in a linear sequence, joined via α-linkages.

name: α-D-Kdo-(2→4)-α-D-Kdo-(2→4)-α-D-Kdo
definition: A trisaccharide consisting of three 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulose residues in a linear sequence, joined via α-linkages.

name: β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)-[α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)]-α-L-Rhap
definition: A branched amino pentasaccharide consisting of four α-L-rhamnose residues (one at the reducing end) and a single β-D-N-acetylglucosamine residue.

name: E. coli strain F576 LPS core oligosaccharide
definition: A branched thirteen-membered oligosaccharide phosphate consisting of two galactose residues, three glucose residues, two 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid residues, three L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose residues and three glucosamine residues, one of which is acetylated and another is at the reducing end. The unit constitutes the core oligosaccharide structure of enterobacterial lipopolysaccharide obtained from E. coli strain F576.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: An aminotrisaccharide consisting of two rhamnose residues and one N-acetylglucosamine residue in a linear sequence, joined via α-linkages.

name: indan-5-ol
definition: A member of the class of phenols that is indan which has been hydroxylated at position 5.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-2-deoxy-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: A trisaccharide consisting of rhamnose, 2-deoxyrhamnose and N-acetylglucosamine residues in a linear sequence, joined via α-linkages.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap
definition: A pentasaccharide consisting of four rhamnose residues (one at the reducing end) and one N-acetylglucosamine residue in a linear sequence, joined via α-linkages.

name: α-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-Galp
definition: A disaccharide consisting of β-D-galactopyranose having a D-galactopyranosyl residue attached at the 4-position via an α-linkage.

name: N-acetyl-4-(N-acetylglucosaminyl)muramoyl-L-alanyl-D-isoglutamine
definition: An N-acetyl-β-D-glycosaminyl glycopeptide consisting of an N-acetyl-β-D-glycosaminyl-(1→4)-N-acetylmuramoyl moiety attached to the amino terminus of the dipeptide L-alanyl-D-isoglutamine.

name: E. coli strain F653 LPS core oligosaccharide 1
definition: A branched twelve-membered oligosaccharide phosphate consisting of one galactose residue, three glucose residues, two 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid residues, three L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose residues and three glucosamine residues, one of which is at the reducing end. The unit constitutes one of the two core oligosaccharide structures of enterobacterial lipopolysaccharide obtained from E. coli strain F653.

name: N-acetyl-D-galactosamine-6-phosphocholine
definition: A galactose phosphate consisting of N-acetyl-D-galactosamine having a choline phosphate group at the 6-position.

name: E. coli strain F2513 LPS core oligosaccharide
definition: A branched twelve-membered oligosaccharide phosphate consisting of three galactose residues, two glucose residues, two 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid residues, three L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose residues and two glucosamine residues, one of which is at the reducing end. The unit constitutes one of the two core oligosaccharide structures of enterobacterial lipopolysaccharide obtained from E. coli strain F470.

name: α-D-Galp-(1→2)-[α-D-Abep-(1→3)]-α-D-Manp
definition: A branched trisaccharide consisting of D-abequose, D-galactose and D-mannose residues joined via α-linkages with mannose at the reducing end.

name: Salmonella enterica sv. Minnesota LPS core oligosaccharide
definition: A branched twelve-membered oligosaccharide phosphate consisting of two galactose residues, three glucose residues, two 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid residues, three L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose residues and two glucosamine residues, one of which is at the reducing end. The unit constitutes the core oligosaccharide structure of enterobacterial lipopolysaccharide obtained from Salmonella enterica sv. Minnesota.

name: β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-[α-D-Glcp-(1→3)]-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap
definition: A branched amino pentasaccharide comprising an acetylated glucosamine residue, a glucose residue and three rhamnose residues, one of which is at the reducing end.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap
definition: An amino octasaccharide comprising two acetylated glucosamine residues and six α-L-rhamnose residues, one of which is at the reducing end.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap
definition: An amino tetrasaccharide comprising an acetylated glucosamine residue and three α-L-rhamnose residues, one of which is at the reducing end.

name: 4,6-dideoxy-4-(2-methoxypropionamido)-3-C,2-O-dimethyl-L-mannopyranosyl-(1→3)-L-fucopyranose
definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of N-(2-methoxypropionyl)kansosamine linked via a glycosidic bond (of unspecified configuration) to O-3 of L-fucose.

name: (R)-carbinoxamine
definition: The (R)- (inactive) enantiomer of carbinoxamine.

name: (S)-carbinoxamine
definition: The (S)- (active) enantiomer of carbinoxamine.

name: (S)-carbinoxamine maleate
definition: The maleic acid salt of (S)-carbinoxamine.

name: mephedrone
definition: An aromatic ketone that is propiophenone substituted at C-4 and at C-β with methyl and methylamino groups respectively. It is a synthetic stimulant and entactogen drug of the amphetamine and cathinone classes.

name: 2-aminopropiophenone
definition: Propiophenone substituted at the β-carbon by an amino group.

name: (R)-carisoprodol
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of carisoprodol.

name: 4-methylpropiophenone
definition: An aromatic ketone that is propiophenone bearing a methyl group at C-4.

name: (S)-carisoprodol
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of carisoprodol.

name: methylamine hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride formed from methylamine.

name: methylammonium
definition: The conjugate acid of methylamine; major species at pH 7.3.

name: cefditoren
definition: A broad spectrum, third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic with (Z)-2-(4-methyl-1,3-thiazol-5-yl)ethenyl and (2Z)-2-(2-amino-1,3-thiazol-4-yl)-2-(methoxyimino)acetamido groups at positions 3 and 7, respectively, of the cephem skeleton. Generally administered as its orally absorbed pivaloyloxymethyl ester prodrug, it is used for the treatment of mild to moderate infections caused by susceptible strains of microorganisms in acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, community-acquired pneumonia, pharyngitis/tonsillitis, and uncomplicated skin and skin-structure infections.

name: α-D-Ko-(2→4)-α-D-Kdo
definition: A disaccharide comprising a D-glycero-α-D-talo-oct-2-ulosonyl unit in (2→4) linkage with 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulopyranonosonic acid; it forms part of the core structure of bacterial lipopolysaccharides.

name: 5,6,7,8-tetrahydrosarcinapterin
definition: The L-glutamide of 5,6,7,8-tetrahydromethanopterin.

name: S-(2-boronoethyl)-L-cysteine
definition: L-cysteine substituted at sulfur by a 2-boronoethyl group.

name: α-D-Kdo-(2→4)-α-D-Ko
definition: A disaccharide comprising a 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulopyranonosonyl unit in (2→4) linkage with D-glycero-α-D-talo-oct-2-ulosonic acid; it is found in the core structure of bacterial lipopolysaccharides.

name: α-D-Ko
definition: An octose sugar sometimes found in Gram-negative bacteria as a lipopolysaccharide constituent, in combination with its 3-deoxy derivative (α-D-Kdo).

name: cefepime(1+)
definition: The conjugate acid of cefepime.

name: 2-hydroxychromene-2-carboxylate
definition: Conjugate base of 2-hydroxy-2H-chromene-2-carboxylic acid.

name: (3E)-4-(2-hydroxyphenyl)-2-oxobut-3-enoate
definition: Conjugate base of (3E)-4-(2-hydroxyphenyl)-2-oxobut-3-enoic acid.

name: (3E)-4-(2-hydroxyphenyl)-2-oxobut-3-enoic acid
definition: A pyruvic acid derivative having a 2-hydroxybenzylidene group attached at the 3-position and E-stereochemistry.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of N-acetyl-β-D-glucosamine having an α-L-rhamnosyl residue attached at the 3-position.

name: 7-(3-methylbut-2-enyl)-L-tryptophan
definition: An L-tryptophan derivative that is the 7-(3,3-dimethylallyl) derivative of L-tryptophan.

name: β-D-GalpNAc-(1→4)-α-D-GalpNAc
definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of N-acetyl-α-D-galactosamine having an N-acetyl-D-galactosaminyl residue attached at the 4-position via a β-linkage. Important epitope forming part of the O-polysaccharides of some Gram-negative bacteria.

name: cefotetan(2−)
definition: The dianion formed by removal of a proton from each of the carboxylic acid groups of cefotetan.

name: scalarin
definition: A scalarane sesterterpenoid lactone, a metabolite of marine sponges of the family Thorectidae (order dictyoceratida).

name: 4,6-(1'-carboxyethylidene)-3-O-methyl-β-D-glucopyranose
definition: A monosaccharide derivative that is β-D-glucopyranose having a methyl group at the 3-position and a 1-carboxyethylidene group masking the 4-and 6-positions.

name: 2,4-di-O-methyl-α-L-fucopyranose
definition: A monosaccharide derivative that is the 2,4-di-O-methyl derivative of α-L-fucopyranose.

name: 4-O-methyl-α-L-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→4)-2-O-methyl-α-L-fucopyranose
definition: A disaccharide derivative consisting of 2-O-methyl-α-L-fucopyranose having a 4-O-methyl-α-L-rhamnopyranosyl residue attached at the 4-position.

name: scalarane
definition: A hypothetical sesterterpene skeleton with a structure based on that of a pentamethyl-D-homoandrostane and the basis for the family of scalarane sesterterpenoids.

name: 4-O-methyl-α-L-rhamnopyranose
definition: A monosaccharide derivative that is the 4-O-methyl derivative of α-L-rhamnopyranose.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-[α-D-Glcp-(1→4)]-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: An amino pentasaccharide that is the core polysaccharide sequence for the O-antigen of the Gram-negative bacterium Shigella flexneri.

name: 4-O-acetyl-2,3-di-O-methyl-α-L-fucopyranosyl-(1→3)-α-L-rhamnopyranose
definition: A glycosylrhamnose derivative consisting of α-L-rhamnopyranose having a 4-O-acetyl-2,3-di-O-methyl-α-L-galactopyranosyl residue attached at the 3-position.

name: 4-O-acetyl-2,3-di-O-methyl-α-L-fucopyranose
definition: A monosaccharide derivative that is the 4-O-acetyl-2,3-di-O-methyl derivative of α-L-fucopyranose.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-[α-D-Glcp-(1→4)]-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-[α-D-Glcp-(1→4)]-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: The branched decasaccharide formed when two molecules of the Shigella flexneri O-antigen core pentasaccharide α-L-Rha-(1→2)-α-L-Rha-(1→3)-[α-D-Glc-(1→4)]-α-L-Rha-(1→3)-β-D-GlcNAc are joined end to end via β-(1→2) linkages.

name: GPL-8
definition: A glycopeptidolipid antigen from clinically prominent members of the Mycobacterium avium serocomplex.

name: GPL-4
definition: A glycopeptidolipid antigen from clinically prominent members of the Mycobacterium avium serocomplex.

name: acetyl-GPL-2
definition: A glycopeptidolipid antigen from clinically prominent members of the Mycobacterium avium serocomplex.

name: GPL-9I
definition: A glycopeptidolipid antigen from clinically prominent members of the Mycobacterium avium serocomplex.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-[α-D-Glcp-(1→4)]-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-[α-D-Glcp-(1→4)]-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-[α-D-Glcp-(1→4)]-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: The pentadecasaccharide formed when three molecules of the Shigella flexneri O-antigen core pentasaccharide α-L-Rha-(1→2)-α-L-Rha-(1→3)-[α-D-Glc-(1→4)]-α-L-Rha-(1→3)-β-D-GlcNAc are joined end to end via β-(1→2) linkages.

name: GPL-26
definition: A glycopeptidolipid antigen from clinically prominent members of the Mycobacterium avium serocomplex.

name: GPL-25
definition: A glycopeptidolipid antigen from clinically prominent members of the Mycobacterium avium serocomplex.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-[α-D-Glcp-(1→4)]-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: A branched tetrasaccharide consisting of an α-L-Rha-(1→3)-α-L-Rha-(1→3)-β-D-GlcNAc trisaccharide chain, to the central rhamnose residue is also linked α(1→4) a D-glucose residue. Derived from the Shigella liposaccharide O-antigen, it has antigenic properties.

name: 2-Me-α-D-Fucp4NAc-(1→4)-β-D-GlcpA
definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of β-D-glucopyranuronic acid having a 4-acetamido-4,6-dideoxy-2-O-methyl-α-L-galactopyranosyl attached at the 4-position.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-[α-D-Glcp-(1→4)]-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap
definition: A branched amino pentasaccharide consisting of a tetrasaccharide chain of α-D-glucose, α-L-rhamnose, N-acetyl-β-D-glucosamine and α-L-rhamnose residues linked sequentially (1→4), (1→3) and (1→2), to the non-reducing rhamnose residue of which is also linked (1→3) a further α-L-rhamnose residue. Derived from the Shigella liposaccharide O-antigen, it shows antigenic properties.

name: Ac-Asp-Glu-Val-Asp-H
definition: A tetrapeptide consisting of two L-aspartic acid residues, an L-glutamyl residue and an L-valine residue with an acetyl group at the N-terminal and with the C-terminal carboxy group reduced to an aldehyde. It is an inhibitor of caspase-3/7.

name: β-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)-D-Galp
definition: An amino trisaccharide consisting of an N-acetyl-D-glucosamine flanked by two D-galactose residues in a linear sequence.

name: α-D-GalpNAc-(1→2)-α-DD-Hepp-(1→6)-α-D-GlcpN
definition: A linear amino trisaccharide consisting of N-acetyl-α-glucosamine, α-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose and α-glucosamine residues linked (1→2) and (1→6) respectively.

name: cephalexin sodium
definition: The sodium salt of cephalexin.

name: cephalexin(1−)
definition: The anion resulting from the removal of a proton from the carboxylic acid group of cephalexin.

name: α-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-D-Glcp
definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of an α-D-glucose residue having an N-acetyl-α-D-glucosaminyl residue attached at the 2-position.

name: β-D-Glcp(1→6)-α-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)-α-L-QuipNAc-(1→3)-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: A linear tetrasaccharide derivative consisting of β-D-glucose, N-acetyl-α-D-fucosamine, N-acetyl-α-L-quinovosamine and N-acetyl-β-D-glucosamine residues linked sequentially (1→6), (1→3) and (1→3). It forms an important epitope of the Proteus vulgaris O-specific polysaccharide.

name: 3-formylbutyl diphosphate
definition: An organic phosphate that is the diphosphate formed from 3-formyl-n-butyl alcohol.

name: glutathione amide
definition: The dicarboxylic acid monoamide arising by formal condensation of the carboxylic acid group of the glycine residue of glutathione with ammonia.

name: α-D-Galp-(1→2)-[α-D-Abep-(1→3)]-α-D-Manp-(1→4)-α-L-Rhap
definition: A branched tetrasaccharide consisting of α-D-galactose, α-D-mannose and α-L-rhamnose residues linked sequentially (1→2) and (1→4), to the mannose residue of which is also linked (1→3) an α-D-abequose residue. The structure constitutes a possible epitope of the O-antigen polysaccharide in Salmonella.

name: glutathione amide disulfide
definition: The disulfide arising by oxidative dimerisation of glutathione amide.

name: α-D-Abep-(1→3)-α-D-Manp-(1→4)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-D-Galp
definition: A tetrasaccharide consisting of α-D-abequose, α-D-mannose, α-L-rhamnose and α-D-galactose residues linked sequentially (1→3), (1→4) and (1→3); epitope of the O-antigen polysaccharide in Salmonella.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-D-Galp-(1→2)-[α-D-Abep-(1→3)]-α-D-Manp-(1→4)-α-L-Rhap
definition: A branched pentasaccharide consisting of α-L-rhamnose, α-D-galactose, α-D-mannose and α-L-rhamnose residues linked sequentially (1→3), (1→2) and (1→4), to the the mannose residue of which is also linked (1→3) an α-D-abequose residue; epitope of the O-antigen polysaccharide in Salmonella.

name: 3-epi-6-deoxocathasterone
definition: The 3-α-hydroxy epimer of 6-deoxocathasterone.

name: (5α,22S,24R)-22-hydroxyergostan-3-one
definition: A brassinosteroid that is 6-deoxocathasterone in which the hydroxy group at position 3 has been oxidised to the corresponding ketone.

name: β-D-mannosyl 4,8,12,16,20-pentamethylheptacosyl phosphate
definition: A fully saturated β-D-mannose polyisoprenoid phosphoglycolipid (C27 chain-length) obtained from Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

name: muramyl dipeptide
definition: A glycopeptide that is N-propionyl-L-alanyl-D-α-glutamine in which the pro-R hydrogen of the propionyl group has been replaced by the oxygen at position 3 of 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-β-D-glucopyranose. A peptidoglycan constituent of both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.

name: L-Thr-(N→6)-α-D-Galp6d3OAc-(1→3)-β-D-GalpNAc
definition: An L-threonine derivative in which L-threonine is linked via its nitrogen to C-6 of the non-reducing-end galactose residue of 3-O-acetyl-α-D-galacto-hexodialdo-1,5-pyranosyl-(1→3)-N-acetyl-acetamido-2-deoxy-β-D-galactosamine; an important threonine-containing epitope of the Proteus penneri O-specific polysaccharide.

name: 1-hexadecanoyl-2-{12-[(7-nitro-2,1,3-benzoxadiazol-4-yl)amino]dodecanoyl}-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine
definition: A 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine in which the acyl groups at C-1 and C-2 are hexadecanoyl and 12-[(7-nitrobenz-2-oxa-1,3-diazol-4-yl)amino]dodecanoyl respectively.

name: 15β-hydroxyprogesterone
definition: Progesterone in which the hydrogen at the 15β position is substituted by a hydroxy group.

name: βD-GlcN4P-(1→6)-α-D-GlcN1P
definition: An amino disaccharide (1,4'-bisphosphorylated glucosamine disaccharide) corresponding to the carbohydrate portion of E. coli J-5 lipid A.

name: 2-O-acetyl-α-L-rhamnose
definition: A monosaccharide derivative that is the 2-O-acetyl derivative of α-L-rhamnose.

name: 1-hexadecanoyl-2-{6-[(7-nitro-2,1,3-benzoxadiazol-4-yl)amino]hexanoyl}-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine
definition: A 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine(1+) in which the acyl groups at C-1 and C-2 are hexadecanoyl and 6-[(7-nitrobenz-2-oxa-1,3-diazol-4-yl)amino]hexanoyl respectively.

name: bromophenol blue
definition: 3H-2,1-Benzoxathiole 1,1-dioxide in which both of the hydrogens at position 3 have been substituted by 3,5-dibromo-4-hydroxyphenyl groups. It is used as a laboratory indicator, changing from yellow below pH 3 to purple at pH 4.6, and as a size marker for monitoring the progress of agarose gel and polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis. It has also been used as an industrial dye.

name: α-D-Glcp-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap2Ac
definition: A linear tetrasaccharide derivative consisting of an α-D-glucosyl residue, two α-L-rhamnosyl residues and a 2-O-acetyl-α-L-rhamnose at the reducing end.

name: N-{6-[(7-nitrobenzo-2,1,3-oxadiazol-4-yl)amino]hexanoyl}sphingosylphosphocholine
definition: A phosphosphingolipid that is sphingosylphosphocholine with the amino nitrogen converted into a 6-{[N-(7-nitrobenzo-2,1,3-oxadiazol-4-yl)amino]}hexananamido group.

name: (9R,13R)-12-oxophytodienoate
definition: Conjugate base of (9R,13R)-12-oxophytodienoic acid.

name: N-{6-[(7-nitro-2,1,3-benzoxadiazol-4-yl)amino]hexanoyl}sphingosine
definition: An N-acylsphingosine that is sphingosine with the amino nitrogen converted into a 6-{[N-(7-nitrobenzo-2,1,3-oxadiazol-4-yl)amino]}hexananamido group.

name: α-D-Galp-(1→3)-β-D-Manp
definition: An α-D-Galp-(1→3)-D-Manp in which the mannopyranose moiety has beta- configuration at the anomeric centre.

name: α-D-Galp-(1→2)-D-Galp
definition: A glycosylgalactose comprising two D-galactose units joined via an α-(1→2) linkage.

name: 2-phospho-L-lactate
definition: The dianion obtained by removal of two acidic protons from 2-phospho-L-lactic acid.

name: L-lactyl-2-diphospho-5'-guanosine(3−)
definition: The trianion obtained by removal of protons from the carboxylic acid and phosphate groups of L-lactyl-2-diphospho-5'-guanosine.

name: L-lactyl-2-diphospho-5'-guanosine
definition: The product from the formal condensation of the alcohol group of L-lactic acid with the terminal phosphate group of guanosine 5'-diphosphate.

name: N4-{N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→2)-α-D-mannosyl-(1→3)-[N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→2)-α-D-mannosyl-(1→6)]-[β-D-xylosyl-(1→2)]-β-D-mannosyl-(1→4)-N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→4)-N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl}-L-asparagine zwitterion
definition: An amino acid zwitterion that is the zwitterionic form of N4-{N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→2)-α-D-mannosyl-(1→3)-[N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→2)-α-D-mannosyl-(1→6)]-[β-D-xylosyl-(1→2)]-β-D-mannosyl-(1→4)-N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→4)-N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl}-L-asparagine.

name: α-L-Fucp-(1→2)-β-D-Galp-(1→3)-[α-L-Fucp-(1→4)]-D-GlcNAc
definition: An amino tetrasaccharide consisting of N-acetylglucosamine having a fucosyl residue attached at the 4-position via a β-linkage and α-fucosyl-(1→2)-galactosyl residues attached at the 3-position, also via a β-linkage.

name: α-L-Fucp-(1→2)-β-D-Galp-(1→3)-[α-L-Fucp-(1→4)]-β-D-GlcpNAc
definition: An α-L-Fucp-(1→2)-β-D-Galp-(1→3)-[α-L-Fucp-(1→4)]-D-GlcNAc where the glucosamine at the reducing end has β-configuration at its anomeric centre; Lewis b.

name: α-L-Fucp-(1→2)-β-D-Galp-(1→3)-[α-L-Fucp-(1→4)]-α-D-GlcNAc
definition: An α-L-Fucp-(1→2)-β-D-Galp-(1→3)-[α-L-Fucp-(1→4)]-D-GlcNAc where the glucosamine at the reducing end has α-configuration at its anomeric centre.

name: α-D-Galp-(1→3)-β-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-Glcp
definition: An α-D-Gal-(1→3)-β-D-Gal-(1→4)-D-Glc having β-configuration at the reducing end anomeric centre.

name: 2,6-dideoxy-4-O-methyl-α-D-arabino-hexopyranosyl-(1→3)-4-O-acetyl-2-O-methyl-α-L-fucopyranose
definition: A disaccharide derivative consisting of 4-O-acetyl-2-O-methyl-α-L-fucose having a 2,6-dideoxy-4-O-methyl-α-D-arabino-hexosyl residue attached at the 3-position.

name: chlormerodrin
definition: Urea in which one of the hydrogens is substituted by a 3-chloromercury-2-methoxyprop-1-yl group. It was formerly used as a diuretic, but more potent and less toxic drugs are now available. Its radiolabelled (197Hg, 203Hg) forms were used in diagnostic aids in renal imaging and brain scans.

name: 1-O-(α-D-galactopyranosyl)-N-tetracosanylphytosphingosine
definition: A glycophytoceramide having an α-D-galactopyranosyl residue at the O-1 position and a tetracosanoyl group attached to the nitrogen.

name: chlormerodrin (197Hg)
definition: Chlormerodrin containing the radioactive isotope 197Hg. It was formerly used as a diagnostic aid in determination of renal function.

name: 1-(5-phosphonato-β-D-ribosyl)-5'-AMP(4−)
definition: A nucleotide-sugar oxoanion arising from deprotonation of all four phosphate OH groups of 1-(5-phospho-β-D-ribosyl)-5'-AMP; major species at pH 7.3.

name: N-[(R)-4-phosphonatopantothenoyl]-L-cysteinate(3−)
definition: Trianion of N-[(R)-4-phosphopantothenoyl]-L-cysteine arising from deprotonation of carboxylic acid and phosphate functions.

name: chlormerodrin (203Hg)
definition: Chlormerodrin containing the radioactive isotope 203Hg. It was formerly used as a diagnostic aid in determination of renal function.

name: β-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)-β-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-Glcp-(1→4)-[α-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-3-PEA-L-α-D-Hepp-(1→3)]-L-α-D-Hepp-(1→5)-α-Kdo
definition: β-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)-β-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-Glcp-(1→4)-[α-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-3-PEA-L-α-D-Hepp-(1→3)]-L-α-D-Hepp-(1→5)-Kdo in which the terminal Kdo residue has α anomeric configuration. A branched octasaccharide corresponding to the core oligosaccharide of N. meningitis L3,7,9 type.

name: β-D-Glcp3,6Me2-(1→4)-α-L-Rhap2,3-Me2
definition: A disaccharide derivative consisting of 2,3-di-O-methyl-α-L-rhamnose having a 3,6-di-O-methyl-β-D-glucosyl residue attached at the 4-position.

name: (R)-chlormezanone
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of chlormezanone.

name: (S)-chlormezanone
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of chlormezanone.

name: β-D-Glcp3,6Me2-(1→4)-α-L-Rhap2,3Me2-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap3Me
definition: A linear trisaccharide derivative consisting of a 3,6-di-O-methylglucose residue linked to a 2,3-di-O-methylrhamnosyl-(1→2)-3-O-methylrhamnose unit.

name: α-L-Rhap2,3Me2-(1→2)-α-L-Rhap3Me
definition: A disaccharide derivative consisting of 3-O-methyl-α-L-rhamnose having a 2,3-di-O-methyl-α-L-rhamnosyl residue attached at the 2-position.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-[β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)]-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-[β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)]-α-L-Rhap
definition: A branched amino hexasaccharide consisting of four α-L-rhamnose residues (one at the reducing end) and two β-D-N-acetylglucosamine residues linked as shown.

name: 4-amino-2-chlorobenzoic acid
definition: 4-Aminobenzoic acid in which one of the hydrogens ortho- to the carboxylic acid group is substituted by chlorine.

name: 3,6-di-O-methyl-β-D-glucose
definition: A monosaccharide derivative that is β-D-glucose in which the hydroxy groups at C-3 and C-6 are methylated.

name: glucose 6-monomycolate
definition: A 6-O-acyl-D-glucose that is the 6-O-[(20E)-2-docosyl-3-hydroxy-39-(nonadecan-2-yloxy)-39-oxononatriacont-20-enoyl] derivative of D-glucopyranose.

name: (20E)-2-docosyl-3-hydroxy-39-(nonadecan-2-yloxy)-39-oxononatriacont-20-enoic acid
definition: A mycolic acid having hydroxy, ester and olefin functions in the side-chain.

name: chloroxine
definition: A monohydroxyquinoline that is quinolin-8-ol in which the hydrogens at positions 5 and 7 have been substituted by chlorine. A synthetic antibacterial prepared by chlorination of quinolin-8-ol, it is used for the treatment of dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis of the scalp.

name: 1-O-(hexadec-1-enyl)-2-O-octadeca-9,12-dienoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine
definition: A 1-(alk-1-enyl)-2-acyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine that is the 1-O-(hexadec-1-enyl)-2-O-octadeca-9,12-dienoyl derivative of sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine.

name: (R)-chlorphenesin
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of chlorphenesin.

name: (S)-chlorphenesin
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of chlorphenesin.

name: α-D-Galp-(1→4)-α-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-Glcp
definition: A trisaccharide consisting of two α-D-galactose residues and a β-D-glucose at the reducing end in a linear sequence and joined by (1→4) linkages.

name: β-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)-β-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-Glcp-(1→4)-{α-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-[α-D-Glcp-(1→3)]-7-PEA-L-α-D-Hepp-(1→3)}-L-α-D-Hepp-(1→5)-α-Kdo
definition: An oligosaccharide phosphate that is a branched nonasaccharide corresponding to the core oligosaccharide of N. meningitis L2 type.

name: α-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-Glcp-(1→4)-β-D-Glcp
definition: A linear tetrasaccharide consisting of two adjacent D-galactose residues and two adjacent β-D-glucose residues (one at the reducing end) joined by (1→4) linkages.

name: L-α-D-Hepp-(1→2)-L-α-D-Hepp-(1→3)-[β-Glcp-(1→4)]-L-α-D-Hepp
definition: A branched tetrasaccharide consisting of three L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptosyl residues (one at the reducing end) and a single β-D-glucosyl residue.

name: β-D-Glcp-(1→4)-L-α-D-Hepp
definition: A disaccharide consisting of a D-glucosyl residue in α-(1→4)-linkage with L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose.

name: β-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)-β-D-Galp
definition: An amino trisaccharide comprising an N-acetyl β-D-glucosaminyl residue flanked by two β-D-galactopyranose residues (one at the reducing end).

name: L-α-D-Hepp-(1→3)-L-α-D-Hepp
definition: A disaccharide consisting of two L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose residues joined by a(1→3)-linkage.

name: 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulopyranosonic acid 5-phosphate
definition: An aldooctose phosphate that is the 5-O-phosphono derivative of 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulopyranosonic acid

name: 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulopyranosonic acid 4-phosphate
definition: An aldooctose phosphate that is the 4-O-phosphono derivative of 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulopyranosonic acid.

name: α-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-L-α-D-Hepp-(1→3)-L-α-D-Hepp
definition: A trisaccharide cmoposed of two L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptopyranose residues and one N-acetyl-D-glucosamine residue, linked as shown; a part of the meningococcal inner core oligosacccharide with independent antigenic properties.

name: β-D-Glcp-(1→4)-[L-α-D-Hepp-(1→3)]-L-α-D-Hepp
definition: A branched trisaccharide consisting of one D-glucose and two L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptopyranose residues (one at the reducing end), linked as shown.

name: β-D-Manp-(1→2)-β-D-Manp-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→2)-α-D-Manp
definition: A linear mannopentaose consisting of five D-mannose residues joined sequentially via two β(1→2) and two α(1→2) linkages with α anomeric configuration at the reducing end.

name: cidofovir dihydrate
definition: The dihydrate of the anhydrous form of cidofovir. A nucleoside analogue, it is an injectable antiviral used for the treatment of cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis in AIDS patients.

name: β-D-galactofuranose
definition: A D-galactofuranose that has β- configuration at the anomeric centre.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-[β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)]-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap
definition: A branched amino tetrasaccharide consisting of three α-L-rhamnose residues linked sequentially (1→2) and (1→3) (one at the reducing end) and a single N-acetyl β-D-glucosaminyl residue linked (1→3) to the central rhamnose.

name: β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap
definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of α-L-rhamnose having an N-acetyl β-D-glucosaminyl residue attached at the 3-position.

name: β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-[β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)]-α-L-Rhap
definition: A branched amino pentasaccharide consisting of three α-L-rhamnose residues [linked sequentially (1→3) and (1→2); one at the reducing end] and two N-acetyl β-D-glucosaminyl residues [one linked (1→3) to the reducing-end rhamnose and the other linked (1→3) to the non-reducing-end rhamnose].

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-[β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)]-α-L-Rhap
definition: A branched amino trisaccharide consisting of two α-L-rhamnose residues [linked (1→2); one at the reducing end] with a single N-acetyl β-D-glucosaminyl residue linked (1→3) to the reducing-end rhamnose.

name: β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-L-Rhap
definition: A linear amino trisaccharide consisting of two adjacent α-L-rhamnose residues (one at the reducing end) and a single N-acetyl β-D-glucosaminyl residue joined to each other via (1→3)-linkages.

name: 2-hydroxy-5-(methylsulfanyl)-3-oxopent-1-enyl phosphate(2−)
definition: Dianion of 2-hydroxy-5-(methylsulfanyl)-3-oxopent-1-en-1-yl phosphate.

name: cilastatin sodium
definition: The monosodium salt of cilastatin. It is an inhibitor of dehydropeptidase I (membrane dipeptidase, 3.4.13.19), an enzyme found in the brush border of renal tubes and responsible for degrading the antibiotic imipenem. Cilastatin sodium is therefore administered with imipenem to prolong the antibacterial effect of the latter by preventing its renal metabolism to microbiologically inactive and potentially nephrotoxic products.

name: cilastatin(1−)
definition: The anion resulting from the removal of a proton from a carboxylic acid group of cilastatin.

name: monodehydro-L-ascorbate(1−)
definition: The conjugate base of monodehydro-L-ascorbic acid arising from deprotonation of the 4-hydroxy group; major species at pH 7.3.

name: cinolazepam
definition: A 1,4-benzodiazepinone compound having a 2-cyanoethyl substituent at the 1-position, a hydroxy substituent at the 3-position, a 2-fluorophenyl group at the 5-position and a chloro substituent at the 7-position, it has general properties similar to those of diazepam and has been used for the short-term management of sleep disorders.

name: β-D-Galp-(1→2)-L-glycero-α-D-manno-Hepp-(1→2)-L-glycero-α-D-manno-Hepp-(1→3)-L-glycero-α-D-manno-Hepp-(1→5)-Kdo
definition: A linear pentasaccharide consisting of a β-D-galactose residue, three L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose residues and (at the reducing end) a 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulopyranosonic acid (Kdo) residue linked sequentially (1→2), (1→2), (1→3) and (1→5); the structure is that of the pentasaccharide epitope from Haemophilus influenzae MAHI 4.

name: L-glycero-α-D-manno-Hepp-(1→2)-L-glycero-α-D-manno-Hepp-(1→3)-L-glycero-α-D-manno-Hepp-(1→5)-α-Kdo
definition: A linear tetrasaccharide consisting of three L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptosyl residues and a 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid (Kdo) residue linked sequentially (1→2), (1→2) and (1→5); corresponds to the tetrasaccharide epitope from Haemophilus influenzae MAHI 3.

name: 1,6:5,9:8,12:11,16-tetraanhydro-2,3,4,10,13,14-hexadeoxy-D-glycero-D-allo-D-gulo-heptadeca-2,13-dienitol
definition: A trans-fused organic heterotetracyclic compound consisting of two fused pyran rings flanked by two oxepan rings.

name: (4Z)-2,8:7,12:11,15:14,18:17,22-pentaanhydro-4,5,6,9,10,13,19,20,21-nonadeoxy-L-arabino-L-allo-L-allo-docosa-4,9,20-trienitol
definition: A trans-fused organic heteropentacyclic compound consisting of an oxacyclooctene, an oxepane, two pyrans and a further oxepane ring fused in a linear sequence.

name: naproxen(1−)
definition: The anion formed from naproxen by loss of a proton from the carboxy group.

name: N-octanoylisoglobotriaosyl ceramide
definition: The N-octanoyl derivative of isoglobotriaosyl ceramide.

name: omocianine
definition: A C7-cyanine dye having symmetrically-substituted 2-indolyl units at each end.

name: 2,6-di-O-(α-D-mannosyl)-1-O-(1,2-di-O-hexadecanoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphono)-1D-myo-inositol
definition: A phosphatidylinositol mannoside having two α-D-mannosyl residues attached at the 2- and 6-positions of the inositol and a 1,2-di-O-hexadecanoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphono group at the 1-position.

name: F420-0(2−)
definition: The dianion of the fragment of coenzyme F420 remaining after formal hydrolytic removal of all of the glutamate residues.

name: F420-0
definition: The fragment of coenzyme F420 remaining after formal hydrolytic removal of all of the glutamate residues.

name: 6-acetyl-2,3,4,5-tetrahydropyridine
definition: A tetrahydropyridine compound, bearing an acetyl group in the 6-position.

name: 6-acetyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydropyridine
definition: A tetrahydropyridine bearing an acetyl group in the 6 position. It is the tautomer of CHEBI:59533

name: coenzyme F420-1
definition: The amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxylic acid group of F420-0 with the amino group of L-glutamic acid.

name: coenzyme α-F420-3
definition: The amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxylic acid group of F420-0 with the amino group of L-γ-glutamyl-L-γ-glutamyl-L-glutamic acid.

name: coenzyme α-F420-3(5−)
definition: The penta-anion obtained by removing protons from the phosphate and carboxylic acid groups of coenzyme α-F420-3.

name: (+)-rolipram
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of rolipram.

name: coenzyme γ-F420-2(4−)
definition: The tetra-anion obtained by removing protons from the phosphate and carboxylic acid groups of coenzyme γ-F420-2.

name: coenzyme F420-1(3−)
definition: The tri-anion obtained by removing protons from the phosphate and carboxylic acid groups of coenzyme F420-1.

name: 2,5-diamino-6-(1-D-ribosylamino)pyrimidin-4(3H)-one 5'-phosphate(2−)
definition: The dianion formed by removal of two protons from the phosphate group of 2,5-diamino-6-(1-D-ribosylamino)pyrimidin-4(3H)-one 5'-phosphate.

name: 2,5-diamino-6-(1-D-ribosylamino)pyrimidin-4(3H)-one 5'-phosphate
definition: 5-O-Phosphono-β-D-ribofuranose in which the hydroxy group at position 1 is substituted by the 6-amino group of 2,5,6-triaminopyrimidin-4(3H)-one.

name: α-L-idopyranose
definition: The α-anomer of L-idopyranose.

name: (2R,3R,23Z,33Z)-3-hydroxy-2-octyldopentaconta-23,33-dienoic acid
definition: An optically active mycolic acid having one hydroxy and two olefin functions at respectively positions 3, 23 and 33 of the side-chain.

name: trans-4-(dimethylphenylsilyl)-N-methylpiperidine N-oxide
definition: A piperidine N-oxide having a dimethylphenylsilyl substituent at the 4-position.

name: N-(tert-butoxycarbonyl)piperidin-2-one
definition: Piperidin-2-one N-protected by t-Boc.

name: 1-ethoxy-1-lithioethene
definition: A vinyllithium compound bearing an ethoxy group at the 1-position.

name: sapropterin
definition: A tetrahydropterin that is 2-amino-5,6,7,8-tetrahydropteridin-4(3H)-one in which a hydrogen at position 6 is substituted by a 1,2-dihydroxypropyl group (6R,1'R,2'S-enantiomer).

name: 5-hydroxyisouric acid anion
definition: The conjugate base of 5-hydroxyisouric acid.

name: β-D-Gal-(1→4)-D-Man
definition: A glycosylmannose comprising a β-D-galactopyranose residue in (1→4) linkage with D-mannopyranose; which can inhibit Leishmania major glycoinositol phospholipid binding by sera from patients with acute cutaneous leishmaniasis.

name: thermospermine
definition: Propane-1,3-diamine in which a hydrogen attached to one nitrogen is substituted by a 3-aminoprop-1-yl group, and a hydrogen attached to the other nitrogen is substituted by a 4-aminobut-1-yl group. A polyamine natural product, its name arises from its similarity to spermine and the fact that it was first isolated from the extreme thermophile, Thermus thermophilus.

name: N-[4-(4-nitrophenylphospho)butanoyl]-L-alanine
definition: An N-[4-(4-nitrophenylphospho)butanoyl]alanine that has S at the chiral carbon.

name: N-[4-(4-nitrophenylphospho)butanoyl]alanine
definition: An alanine derivative having a 4-(4-nitrophenylphospho)butanoyl group attached to the nitrogen of alanine.

name: (R)-clenbuterol
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of clenbuterol.

name: (S)-clenbuterol
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of clenbuterol.

name: (R)-clenbuterol hydrochloride
definition: The monohydrochoride salt of (R)-clenbuterol.

name: (S)-clenbuterol hydrochloride
definition: The monohydrochloride salt of (S)-clenbuterol.

name: α-Neu9,NAc2-(2→6)-GalNAc
definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of an N-acetylglucosamine having an N-acetyl-9-O-acetylneuraminic acid attached via an α-(2→6)-linkage.

name: (1→2)-β-D-mannan
definition: A mannan consisting of repeating mannosyl units joined via β-(1→2)-linkages.

name: 3,6-di-O-methyl-β-D-glucopyranosyl-(1→4)-α-L-rhamnopyranose
definition: A disaccharide derivative consisting of α-L-rhamnose having a 3,6-di-O-methyl-β-D-glucosyl residue attached at the 4-position; corresponds to the carbohydrate portion of synthetic antigens containing the Mycobacterium leprae-specific epitope.

name: α-D-Galp-(1→6)-D-Galp
definition: A glycosylgalactose consisting of D-galactose having an α-D-galactosyl residue attached at the 6-position.

name: Man(a1-2)Man(a1-2)Man(a1-3)[Man(a1-2)Man(a1-3)[Man(a1-2)Man(a1-6)]Man(a1-6)]Man(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-4)GlcNAc
definition: A branched N-glycan derivative that is an undecasaccharide derivative consisting of nine D-mannosyl residues and two N-acetylglucosamine residues (one at the reducing end).

name: β-D-Galp-(1→3)-[α-L-Fucp-(1→4)]-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→3)-β-D-Galp-(1→4)-β-D-Glcp
definition: A branched amino pentasaccharide consisting of two D-glucose residues (one at the reducing end), one N-acetyl-D-glucosamine residue, one D-galactose residue and one L-fucose residue, linked as shown.

name: α-D-Galp-(1→2)-[α-D-Abep-(1→3)]-α-D-Manp-(1→4)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-D-Galp-(1→2)-[α-D-Abep-(1→3)]-α-D-Manp-(1→4)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-D-Galp-(1→2)-[α-D-Abep-(1→3)]-α-D-Manp-(1→4)-α-L-Rhap
definition: A polysaccharide that is a branched dodecasaccharide consisting of three repeating tetrasaccharide units; reported to be a possible epitope of the O-antigen polysaccharide in Salmonella.

name: clocortolone
definition: 16α-Methylpregna-1,4-diene-3,20-dione bearing hydroxy substituents at the 11β and 21 positions, fluorine at position 6 and chlorine at position 9. A medium potency corticosteroid, it is used as its 21-O-pivalate or caproate ester for the relief of inflammatory and pruritic (itching) skin disorders.

name: clocortolone pivalate
definition: The 21-O-pivalate ester of clocortolone. It is used for the relief of inflammatory and pruritic (itching) skin disorders.

name: α-D-Manp-(1→2)-D-Manp
definition: A glycosylmannose consisting of D-mannose having an α-D-mannosyl residue attached at the 2-position.

name: clondronate(2−)
definition: The dianion resulting from the removal of two protons from clondronic acid.

name: clodronic acid disodium salt
definition: The disodium salt of clodronic acid. It inhibits bone resorption and soft tissue calcification, and is used (generally as the tetrahydrate) as an adjunct in the treatment of severe hypercalcaemia associated with malignancy, and in the management of osteolytic lesions and bone pain associated with skeletal metastases.

name: disodium clodronate tetrahydrate
definition: The tetrahydrate of the disodium salt of clodronic acid. It inhibits bone resorption and soft tissue calcification, and is used as an adjunct in the treatment of severe hypercalcaemia associated with malignancy, and in the management of osteolytic lesions and bone pain associated with skeletal metastases.

name: clomocycline
definition: Tetracycline in which the hydrogen at position 7 is substituted by chlorine and a hydrogen attached to the amide nitrogen is substituted by a hydroxymethyl group. A tetracyline antibiotic, it is used to treat acne, urinary tract infections, gum disease, and other bacterial infections such as gonorrhoea and chlamydia.

name: clorazepic acid anion
definition: The anion resulting from the removal of a proton from the carboxylic acid group of clorazepic acid.

name: clorazepate monopotassium
definition: The potassium salt of clorazepic acid.

name: 5-aminoisatin
definition: Isatin substituted at C-5 by an amino group.

name: α-D-Kdo-(2→4)-α-D-Kdo-(2→4)-α-D-Kdo-(2→6)-β-D-GlcN4P-(1→6)-α-D-GlcN1P
definition: An amino pentasaccharide antigen consisting of three 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulose residues and two glucosamine residues (one at the reducing end) in a linear sequence, with two phosphate groups attached.

name: patent blue V
definition: An iminium ion that is a dark bluish synthetic dye used as a food colouring agent

name: colestipol hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride of colestipol, a highly cross-linked, high molecular weight copolymer of diethylenetriamine and epichlorohydrin (hydrochloride), with approximately 1 out of 5 amine nitrogens protonated. It is used for binding bile acids in the intestine, inhibiting their reabsorption.

name: ammonium hexachloroplatinate
definition: An ammonium salt comprising separate ammonium cations and octahedral [PtCl6]2− anions.

name: Disperse Blue 124
definition: A monoazo compound consisting of diazene with a 5-nitrothiazol-2-yl group attached to one nitrogen and a substituted 4-aminophenyl group attached to the other; used as a dye standard for the assay of allergy-releasing dyes in textiles.

name: sodium hexachloroplatinate
definition: An inorganic sodium salt comprising separate sodium cations and octahedral [PtCl6]2− anions.

name: quaternium-15
definition: A quaternary ammonium salt derived from hexamethylenetetramine; used as a preservative in many cosmetics and industrial substances. Also acts as a disinfectant and allergenic agent.

name: sodium tetrachloroplatinate
definition: An inorganic sodium salt comprising separate sodium cations and square planar [PtCl4]2− anions.

name: diclofenac β-D-glucosiduronic acid
definition: A β-D-glucosiduronic acid (β-D-glucuronide) that is a metabolite of diclofenac.

name: 4'-hydroxydiclofenac quinone imine
definition: A quinone imine that is a metabolite of diclofenac arising from 4'-hydroxylation followed by oxidation.

name: 5-hydroxydiclofenac quinone imine
definition: A quinone imine that is a metabolite of diclofenac arising from 5-hydroxylation followed by oxidation.

name: 5-hydroxydiclofenac
definition: A monocarboxylic acid that is the 5-hydroxylated metabolite of diclofenac.

name: 4'-hydroxydiclofenac
definition: A monocarboxylic acid that is the 4'-hydroxylated metabolite of diclofenac.

name: β-D-Galp6P-(1→4)-α-D-Manp
definition: A disaccharide phosphate corresponding to part of the oligosaccharide repeating unit of Leishmania major promastigote lipophosphoglycan.

name: β-D-Galp-(1→3)-β-D-Galp6P-(1→4)-α-D-Manp
definition: An oligosaccharide phosphate corresponding to the oligosaccharide repeating unit of Leishmania major promastigote lipophosphoglycan.

name: β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→3)-[β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→6)]-[β-D-Xylp-(1→2)]-β-D-Manp-(1→4)-β-D-GlcpNAc-(1→4)-[α-L-Fucp-(1→3)]-D-GlcpNAc
definition: A highly branched amino nonasaccharide consisting of a D-GlcNAc residue at the reducing end with a β-D-GlcNAc-(1→2)-α-D-Man-(1→3)-[β-D-GlcNAc-(1→2)-α-D-Man-(1→6)]-[β-D-Xyl-(1→2)]-β-D-Man-(1→4)-β-D-GlcNAc moiety attached via a β-(1→4)-linkage and an L-Fuc residue attached via an α-(1→3)-linkage. Found on Cry j 1, the major allergen of Cryptomeria japonica pollen.

name: α-L-Araf-(1→2)-β-D-Galp-(1→3)-β-D-Galp6P-(1→4)-α-D-Manp
definition: A tetrasaccharide derivative that is the tetrasaccharide phosphate corresponding to the oligosaccharide repeating unit of Leishmania major promastigote lipophosphoglycan.

name: α-D-Manp-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→3)-α-D-Manp-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→2)-D-Manp
definition: A linear hexasaccharide consisting of D-mannosyl residues connected exclusively by α-linkages, obtained from acetolysis of Candida parapsilosis cell-wall D-mannan.

name: β-D-Galp-(1→3)-β-D-Galp-(1→3)-β-D-Galp-(1→3)-β-D-Galp6P-(1→4)-α-D-Manp
definition: A pentasaccharide derivative that is a pentasaccharide phosphate epitope from Leishmania major promastigote lipophosphoglycan.

name: GPL-1
definition: A glycopeptidolipid antigen from clinically prominent members of the Mycobacterium avium serocomplex.

name: L-lysyl-D-alanine
definition: A dipeptide formed from L-lysyl and D-alanyl residues.

name: L-lysyl-D-alanyl-D-alanine
definition: A linear tripeptide comprised of one L-lysine residue and two D-alanyl residues.

name: (5R)-5-isopropenyl-2-methylcyclohexane 1-hydroperoxide
definition: A peroxol (hydroperoxide) derived from (R)-limonene.

name: (5R)-5-isopropenyl-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane 1-hydroperoxide
definition: A peroxol (hydroperoxide) obtained from (−)-carvone via sequential methylenation and hydroperoxidation.

name: β-D-Manp-(1→2)-β-D-Manp-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→2)-α-D-Manp-(1→2)-D-Manp
definition: A linear hexasaccharide consisting of D-mannosyl residues connected by two β- and three α-1,2-linkages, obtained from Candida albicans cell-wall D-mannan.

name: 4-isopropyl-1-methylcyclohexane 1-hydroperoxide
definition: A peroxol (hydroperoxide) that is the 1-hydroperoxy derivative of p-menthane.

name: N-ethylsuccinimide-mycothiol conjugate
definition: A mycothiol conjugate arising from formal addition of the side-chain sulfur atom of the cysteine residue of mycothiol across the C=C double bond of N-ethylmaleimide.

name: acetophenone-mycothiol conjugate
definition: The S-conjugate of mycothiol and acetophenone.

name: β-D-mannosyl 3,7,11,15,19,23,27,31-octamethyldotriacontyl phosphate
definition: A fully saturated D-mannose polyisoprenoid phosphoglycolipid (C32 chain-length) obtained from Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

name: N-acetyl-S-phenacyl-L-cysteine
definition: The S-phenacyl derivative of N-acetyl-L-cysteine.

name: N-acetyl-S-(N-ethylsuccinimido)-L-cysteine
definition: An S-substituted N-acetyl-L-cysteine arising from formal 1,4-addition of the side-chain sulfur atom to N-ethylmaleimide.

name: PIM6
definition: A phosphatidylinositol mannoside having the phosphatidyl moiety (with specific O-acyl groups) at the 1-position, a single mannosyl residue at the 2-position and a linear pentamannoside at position 6 of the inositol ring.

name: S-nitrosomycothiol
definition: The S-nitroso derivative of mycothiol.

name: mycothiol sulfinamide
definition: The sulfinamide of mycothiol.

name: 5-(6-aminohexanamido)isatin
definition: Isatin bearing a 6-aminohexanamido group at C-5.

name: α-L-Rhap-(1→2)-L-Rhap
definition: A glycosylrhamnose consisting of two L-rhamnopyranose units joined by an α(1→2) linkage.

name: bisphenol A (3-chloro-2-hydroxypropyl) (2,3-dihydroxypropyl) ether
definition: The (3-chloro-2-hydroxypropyl) (2,3-dihydroxypropyl) diether of bisphenol A; a small molecule that inhibits transactivation of the AR amino-terminal domain (NTD).

name: GPL-21
definition: A glycopeptidolipid antigen from clinically prominent members of the Mycobacterium avium serocomplex

name: precursor Z(1−)
definition: The anion resulting from the removal of the proton from the phosphate group of precursor Z.

name: amorolfine hydrochloride
definition: A hydrochloride resulting from the formal reacton of equimolar amounts of hydrogen chloride and amorolfine. An inhibitor of the action of squalene monooxygenase, Δ14 reductase and D7-D8 isomerase and an antifungal agent, it is used for the topical treatment of fungal nail and skin infections.

name: arseno-mycothiol
definition: The dihydrogen arsenothioate resulting from the formal condensation of the thiol group of mycothiol with arsenic acid.

name: prolinol
definition: An amino alcohol formed by reduction of the amino acid proline.

name: arseno-mycothiol(1−)
definition: The anion resulting from the removal of a proton from the arsenate group of arseno-mycothiol.

name: arseno-mycothiol(2−)
definition: The dianion resulting from the removal of both protons from the arsenate group of arseno-mycothiol.

name: [5-fluoro-1-(4-isopropylbenzylidene)-2-methylinden-3-yl]acetic acid
definition: A sulindac-based non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug.

name: colistin A sodium methanesulfonate
definition: Colistin A in which each of the primary amino groups is converted into the corresponding aminomethanesulfonic acid sodium salt, commonly by treatment with formaldehyde followed by sodium bisulfite.

name: colistin B sodium methanesulfonate
definition: Colistin B in which each of the primary amino groups is converted into the corresponding aminomethanesulfonic acid sodium salt, commonly by treatment with formaldehyde followed by sodium bisulfite.

name: colistimethate A(5−)
definition: The penta-anion resulting from the removal of protons from each of the sulfonic acid groups of colistimethate A.

name: colistimethate B(5−)
definition: The penta-anion resulting from the removal of protons from each of the sulfonic acid groups of colistimethate B.

name: colistimethate A
definition: Colistin A in which each of the primary amino groups is converted to the corresponding aminomethanesulfonic acid, commonly by the action of formaldehyde followed by sodium bisulfite.

name: colistimethate B
definition: Colistin B in which each of the primary amino groups is converted into the corresponding aminomethanesulfonic acid, commonly by the action of formaldehyde followed by sodium bisulfite.

name: colistin B
definition: A polymyxin having a 6-methylheptanoyl group at the amino terminus.

name: colistin A sulfate
definition: The sulfuric acid salt of colistin A.

name: colistin B sulfate
definition: The sulfuric acid salt of colistin B.

name: (1-hydroxycyclopentyl)phenylacetic acid
definition: (1-hydroxycyclopentyl)acetic acid in which one of the hydrogens α to the carboxylic acid group is substituted by a phenyl group.

name: edaxadiene
definition: A bicyclic halimane-type diterpenoid produced by the pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis as a defense against macrophage attack. The structure was revised in 2010, having been initially thought to be tricyclic. The compound was originally named nosyberkol after it was first isolated in 2004 from a sponge, Raspailia sp., collected from the Nosy Be island of Madagascar.

name: halimane
definition: A diterpene that consists of decalin bearing four methyl substituents at positions 1, 2, 5 and 5 as well as a 3-methylpentyl substituent at position 1.

name: (R)-cyclopentolate
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of cyclopentolate.

name: (S)-cyclopentolate
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of cyclopentolate.

name: (R)-cyclopentolate hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of (R)-cyclopentolate.

name: (S)-cyclopentolate hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of (S)-cyclopentolate.

name: cycrimine
definition: A member of the class of piperidines that is 3-(piperidin-1-yl)propan-1-ol in which one of the hydrogen atoms at the 1-position is substituted by cyclopentyl, and the other is substituted by phenyl. A central anticholinergic, it is used as its hydrochloride salt in the management and treatment of Parkinson's disease.

name: cycrimine hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of cycrimine. A central anticholinergic, it is used as its hydrochloride salt in the management and treatment of Parkinson's disease.

name: (4aS,5R,9R,11S)-1,1,5,8,11-pentamethyl-8-vinyl-1,2,3,4,4a,5,6,7,8,9-decahydro-5,9-methanobenzocyclooctene
definition: A halimane-diterpenoid structure originally proposed as the structure for edaxadiene (CHEBI:59685).

name: cyproheptadine hydrochloride (anhydrous)
definition: The hydrochloride salt of cyproheptadine. Note that the drug named cyproheptadine hydrochloride generally refers to cyproheptadine hydrochloride sesquihydrate.

name: dantrolene(1−)
definition: The organic anion resulting from the removal of a proton from the hydrogen-bearing nitrogen atom of dantrolene.

name: 2,2':6',2'':6'',2''':6''',2'''':6'''',2'''''-sexipyridine
definition: A linear sexipyridine in which six unsubstituted pyridine units are linked by five 2:6'-linkages.

name: sexipyridine
definition: A cyclic sexipyridine in which six unsubstituted pyridine units are linked by six 2:6'-linkages

name: (R)-cycrimine
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of cycrimine.

name: (S)-cycrimine
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of cycrimine.

name: (R)-cycrimine hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of (R)-cycrimine.

name: (S)-cycrimine hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of (S)-cycrimine.

name: hydrogensquarate
definition: A carbon oxoanion which is a monoanion obtained by the deprotonation of one of the hydroxy groups of squaric acid.

name: squarate
definition: A carbon oxoanion which is the dianion obtained by the deprotonation of the hydroxy group of hydrogensquarate.

name: Δ1-dihydrotestosterone
definition: An anabolic steroid that differs from testosterone by having a 1,2-double bond instead of a 4,5-double bond in its A ring. A potent androgen with anabolic properties, it was legally sold as a prohormone in the U.S.A. until 2005, when it was reclassified as a Schedule III drug.

name: sodium squarate
definition: An organic sodium salt which is the disodium salt of squaric acid.

name: lithium squarate
definition: An organic lithium salt which is the dilithium salt of squaric acid.

name: demarcarium
definition: The bis(quaternary ammonium) dication obtained by N,N'-dimethylation of the N,N'-bis[3-(dimethylamino)phenyl carbamate] derivative of 2,13-diazatetradecane.

name: prop-1-ene-1-thiol
definition: The thioenol of propene.

name: demeclocycline hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of demeclocycline. A tetracycline antibiotic, it is used (mainly as the hydrochloride) for the treatment of Lyme disease, acne and bronchitis, as well as for hyponatraemia (low blood sodium concentration) due to the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH) where fluid restriction alone has been ineffective.

name: desmopressin acetate trihydrate
definition: The trihydrate of the acetic acid salt of desmopressin. An antidiuretic, it increases urine concentration and decreases urine production, and is used to prevent and control excessive thirst, urination, and dehydration caused by injury, surgery, and certain medical conditions. It is also used in the diagnosis and treatment of cranial diabetes insipidus and in tests of renal function.

name: fenfluramine hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of fenfluramine. It binds to the serotonin reuptake pump, causing inhbition of serotonin uptake and release of serotonin. The resulting increased levels of serotonin lead to greater serotonin receptor activation which in turn lead to enhancement of serotoninergic transmission in the centres of feeding behavior located in the hypothalamus. This suppresses the appetite for carbohydrates. Fenfluramine hydrochloride was used for treatment of diabetes and obesity. It was withdrawn worldwide after reports of heart valve disease and pulmonary hypertension.

name: (S)-fenfluramine hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of (S)-fenfluramine. It stimulates the release of serotonin and selectively inhibits its reuptake, but unlike the racemate it does not possess catecholamine agonist activity. It was formerly given by mouth in the treatment of obesity, but, like the racemate, was withdrawn wolrdwide following reports of valvular heart defects.

name: amidotrizoic acid anion
definition: The anion obtained by removal of the proton from the carboxylic acid group of amidotrizoic acid.

name: N-methylglucamine
definition: A hexosamine that is D-glucitol in which the hydroxy group at position 1 is substituted by the nitrogen of a methylamino group. A crystalline base, it is used in preparing salts of certain acids for use as diagnostic radiopaque media, while its antimonate is used as an antiprotozoal in the treatment of leishmaniasis.

name: amidotrizoic acid dihydrate
definition: The dihydrate form of amidotrizoic acid. Both the dihydrate and the anhydrous form are used as X-ray contrast media.

name: cinchocaine hydrochloride
definition: The monohydrochloride salt of cinchocaine. It is used in creams, ointments and suppositories for temporary relief of pain and itching associated with skin and anorectal conditions.

name: trans-cinnamyl methyl 2-tosylmalonate
definition: A tosylmalonate ester in which the esterifying groups are methyl and trans-cinnamyl.

name: 1,1'-bi(cyclohexyl)-1-carboxylic acid
definition: Cyclohexanecarboxylic acid in which the hydrogen attached to the α-carbon is substituted by a cyclohexyl group.

name: N-methoxy-N-methylbenzamide
definition: The Weinreb amide of benzoic acid.

name: (R)-diethylpropion
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of amfepramone.

name: (S)-diethylpropion
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of amfepramone.

name: phosphoramidous acid
definition: A derivative of phosphorous acid in which one of the acidic hydroxy groups has been replaced by amino.

name: diflorasone
definition: The 16β-analogue of flumethasone. It is used as the 17,21-diacetate as a topical anti-inflammatory and antipruritic in the treatment of various skin disorders.

name: dihydroergotamine mesylate
definition: The methanesulfonic acid salt of dihydroergotamine, a semisynthetic ergot alkaloid with weaker oxytocic and vasoconstrictor properties than ergotamine. Both the mesylate and the tartrate salts are used for the treatment of migraine and orthostatic hypotension.

name: dihydroergotamine tartrate
definition: The L-(+)-tartaric acid salt of dihydroergotamine, a semisynthetic ergot alkaloid with weaker oxytocic and vasoconstrictor properties than ergotamine. Both the tartrate and the mesylate salts are used for the treatment of migraine and orthostatic hypotension.

name: ethyl hydrogen phosphate(1−)
definition: An organophosphate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of ethyl dihydrogen phosphate arising from deprotonation of one of the OH groups of the phosphate.

name: ethyl phosphate(2−)
definition: An organophosphate oxoanion that is the dianion of ethyl phosphate arising from deprotonation of both OH groups of the phosphate.

name: methyl phosphate(2−)
definition: Dianion of methyl phosphate arising from deprotonation of both OH groups of the phosphate.

name: N-(5'-phosphonatopyridoxyl)-D-alaninate(2−)
definition: An organophosphate oxoanion that is the dianion of N-(5'-phosphopyridoxyl)-D-alanine having anionic carboxy, hydroxy and phosphate groups with the secondary amino group and pyridine nitrogen protonated.

name: N-(5'-phosphonatopyridoxyl)-L-alaninate(2−)
definition: An organophosphate oxoanion that is the dianion of N-(5'-phosphopyridoxyl)-L-alanine having anionic carboxy, hydroxy and phosphate groups with the secondary amino group and pyridine nitrogen protonated.

name: N6-acetyl-N2-(5'-phosphonatopyridoxyl)-L-lysinate(2−)
definition: An organophosphate oxoanion that is the dianion of N6-acetyl-N2-(5'-phosphopyridoxyl)-L-alanine having anionic carboxy, hydroxy and phosphate groups with the secondary amino group and pyridine nitrogen protonated.

name: N6-acetyl-N2-(5'-phosphopyridoxyl)-L-lysine
definition: A N6-acyl-L-lysine arising from reductive N-alkylation of N6-acetyl-L-lysine by pyridoxal-5-phosphate.

name: 8-chlorotheophylline
definition: 1,3-Dimethylxanthine in which the hydrogen at position 8 is substituted by chlorine.

name: cromoglycic acid
definition: A dicarboxylic acid that is the bis-chromone derivative of glycerol. It is effective as a mast cell stabilizer.

name: cromoglycate(1−)
definition: The monocarboxylate anion of cromoglycic acid.

name: D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate(2−)
definition: Dianion of D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate arising from deprotonation of both OH groups of the phosphate.

name: 8-chlorotheophylline(1−)
definition: The anion resulting from the removal of the proton fron the purine ring of 8-chlorotheophylline.

name: dimethylthiambutene
definition: N,N-Dimethylbut-3-en-2-amine in which each of the hydrogens at position 4 is substituted by a 2-thienyl group. An opioid analgesic drug, it is controlled under the UN Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs (1961), but is used in veterinary medicine, particularly in Japan.

name: diphemanil methylsulfate
definition: The alkene resulting from the formal Wittig olefination of benzophenone and 1,1-dimethyl-4-bromopiperidinium methylsulfate. A quaternary ammonium anticholinergic, it binds muscarinic acetycholine receptors and thereby decreases secretory excretion of stomach acids, saliva and sweat, It is used topically in the treatment of hyperhidorsis (excessive sweating).

name: 2-hydroxy-4-methylvaleric acid
definition: A valeric acid derivative having a hydroxy substituent at the 2-position and a methyl substituent at the 4-position; an α-hydroxy analogue of leucine. A bacterial metabolite, it has also been isolated from amniotic fluid, was found in a patient with dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase deficiency and is present in the urine of patients with short bowel syndrome.

name: diphenoxylate hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of diphenoxylate.

name: thioacrolein
definition: Acrolein in which oxygen has been replaced by divalent sulfur.

name: diphenylpyraline
definition: A member of the class of piperidines that is the benzhydryl ether derivative of 1-methyl-4-hydroxypiperidine. A sedating antihistamine, it is used as the hydrochloride for the symptomatic relief of allergic conditions including rhinitis and hay fever, and in pruritic skin disorders. It is also used as the teoclate salt (piprinhydrinate) as an ingredient in compound preparations for the symptomatic relief of coughs and the common cold.

name: S-adenosyl-L-methionine zwitterion
definition: A zwitterionic tautomer of S-adenosyl-L-methionine arising from shift of the proton from the carboxy group to the amino group.

name: difenoxin hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of difenoxin. It has similar actions and uses to diphenoxylate hydrochloride, being administered for the symptomatic treatment of acute and chronic diarrhoea. In an attempt to discourage abuse (at high doses, difenoxin acts like morphine), preparations usually contain subclinical amounts of atropine sulfate.

name: gibberellin A3 O-β-D-glucoside(1−)
definition: Conjugate base of gibberellin A3 O-β-D-glucoside arising from deprotonation of the carboxylic acid group

name: (R)-dobutamine
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of dobutamine.

name: (S)-dobutamine
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of dobutamine.

name: (S)-nicotinium(1+)
definition: The conjugate acid of (S)-nicotine arising from selective protonation of the tertiary amino group; major species at pH 7.3.

name: (24R,25R)-3α,7α,12α,24-tetrahydroxy-5β-cholestan-26-oyl-CoA(4−)
definition: Tetraanion of (24R,25R)-3α,7α,12α,24-tetrahydroxy-5β-cholestan-26-oyl-CoA arising from deprotonation of phosphate and diphosphate OH groups.

name: docetaxel trihydrate
definition: The trihydrate form of docetaxel. It is used for the treatment of breast, ovarian, and non-small cell lung cancer, and with prednisone or prednisolone in hormone-refractory metastatic prostate cancer.

name: acetyl diphosphate
definition: The ester or anhydride formed by condensation between diphosphoric and acetic acids.

name: domperidone maleate
definition: The maleic acid salt of domperidone. A dopamine antagonist, domperidone is used as an antiemetic for the short-term treatment of nausea and vomiting, and to control gastrointestinal effects of dopaminergic drugs given in the management of parkinsonism. The maleate salt is used in tablet preparations, while the free base is used in oral suspensions.

name: 2,3,5,6-tetrachlorophenolate
definition: A phenolate anion that is the conjugate base of 2,3,5,6-tetrachlorophenol, arising from deprotonation of the acidic phenol function.

name: meso-doxacurium
definition: The (1R,1'S,2S,2'R) isomer of 2,2'-[(1,4-dioxobutane-1,4-diyl)bis(oxypropane-3,1-diyl)]bis[6,7,8-trimethoxy-2-methyl-1-(3,4,5-trimethoxybenzyl)-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinolinium]. It is the meso-isomer which has a trans configuration at the 1 and 2 positions of the tetrahydroisoquinolinium rings.

name: meso-doxacurium chloride
definition: The dichloride salt of meso-doxacurium.

name: (1R,2S,1'R,2'S)-doxacurium
definition: The (1R,2S,1'R,2'S)-diastereoisomer of doxacurium.

name: (1R,2S,1'R,2'S)-doxacurium chloride
definition: The dichloride salt of (1R,2S,1'R,2'S)-doxacurium.

name: (1S,2R,1'S,2'R)-doxacurium
definition: The (1S,2R,1'S,2'R)-diastereoisomer of doxacurium.

name: (1S,2R,1'S,2'R)-doxacurium chloride
definition: The dichloride salt of (1S,2R,1'S,2'R)-doxacurium.

name: [(1E)-3,3-dimethyl-1-(4,4,5,5-tetramethyl-1,3,2-dioxaborolan-2-yl)but-1-en-1-yl]zirconocene chloride
definition: A gem-borazirconocene in which the two cyclopentadienyl rings, Cl, and C(sp2) bonded to a dioxaborolanyl system are coordinated to the zirconium atom.

name: CMP-3-deoxy-α-D-manno-octulosonate(2−)
definition: A doubly-charged nucleotide-sugar oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the carboxylic acid and phosphate functions of CMP-3-deoxy-α-D-manno-octulosonic acid.

name: agrocybin
definition: A triyne amide produced by the Brazilian fungus Agrocybe perfecta (Basidiomycota).

name: doxapram hydrochloride (anhydrous)
definition: The hydrochloride salt of doxapram. A central and respiratory stimulant with a brief duration of action, both doxapram hydrochloride and its hydrate are used as a temporary treatment of acute respiratory failure, particularly when superimposed on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and of postoperative respiratory depression. It has also been used for treatment of postoperative shivering.

name: glyoxamide
definition: The simplest of the class of glyoxamides, with no substitution on nitrogen.

name: (R)-doxapram
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of doxapram.

name: (S)-doxapram
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of doxapram.

name: (R)-dyphylline
definition: The (R)-enantiomer of dyphylline.

name: (S)-dyphylline
definition: The (S)-enantiomer of dyphylline.

name: ecothiopate iodide
definition: The iodide salt of ecothiopate. An irreversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, it is used an ocular antihypertensive in the treatment of open-angle glaucoma, particularly when other drugs have proved inadequate.

name: benzyl bromide
definition: A member of the class of benzyl bromides that is toluene substituted on the α-carbon with bromine.

name: myrophine
definition: The 3-O-benzyl and 6-myristyl derivative of morphine, for which it is a prodrug. Myrophine is almost invariably used as the hydrochloride.

name: β-D-Gal-(1→4)-α-D-Glc-(1→3)-[α-D-GlcNAc-(1→2)]-α-L-Hep
definition: An amino tetrasaccharide and epitope consisting of L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptopyranose having a lactosyl moiety attached at the 3-position via an α-linkage and an α-N-acetylglucosaminyl residue at the 2-position.

name: myrophine hydrochloride
definition: The hydrochloride salt of myrophine.

name: D-fructofuranuronate
definition: The conjugate base of D-fructofuranuronic acid.

name: emedastine difumarate
definition: The fumaric acid salt of emedastine containing two molecules of fumaric acid for each molecule of emedastine. A relatively selective histamine H1 antagonist, it is used for allergic rhinitis, urticaria, and pruritic skin disorders, and in eyedrops for the symptomatic relief of allergic conjuntivitis.

name: 3-O-α-abequopyranosyl-α-D-mannopyranose
definition: A glycosylmannose consisting of α-D-mannopyranose having an α-abequopyranosyl residue attached at the 3-position.

name: α-D-Galp-(1→2)-[α-Abep-(1→3)]-α-D-Manp-(1→4)-α-L-Rhap-(1→3)-α-D-Galp-(1→2)-[α-Abep-(1→3)]-α-D-Manp-(1→4)-α-L-Rhap
definition: A branched octasaccharide consisting of two repeating tetrasaccharide units; isolated from phage P22 endo-rhamnosidase cleaved S. typhimurium O-polysaccharide chains.

name: pandangolide 1
definition: A hexaketide lactone isolated from the sponge-associated fungus Cladosporium sp. It is a diastereoisomer of pandangolide 1a.

name: pandangolide 1a
definition: A hexaketide lactone isolated from the sponge-associated fungus Cladosporium sp. It is a diastereoisomer of pandangolide 1.

name: enalaprilat dihydrate
definition: The dihydrate form of enalaprilat, an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor that is used (often in the form of its prodrug, enalapril) in the treatment of hypertension and heart failure, for reduction of proteinuria and renal disease in patients with nephropathies, and for the prevention of stroke, myocardial infarction, and cardiac death in high-risk patients. Unlike enalapril, enalaprilat is not absorbed by mouth but is administered by intravenous injection.

name: aloesone
